reviews.text: Very cute art style with snappy controls. I'm just getting started but I can tell there is a lot of depth, especially with the dynamic meta feature! Highly recommended

Such a cute game with style and characters you just want to have minis or plush of. It's great to second screen and has a depth that creeps up on you with the in-game economy. Hard to put down when you start climbing the leaderboard. A little tricky to get into at the very start with some frustrating battles to make sense of the mechanics if you haven't auto battled before. But very clear and easy to use minions with skills that can never truely be unbalanced due to the cool economy mechanic. Runs on just about anything, and has good optimization. A little rough around the sound effects and the ui could use just a little more skeumorphism to help interact with it. If you want something on the side, or love autobattlers and need something that has longevity and has a lot of promis for more, this is a must try.

I've played a lot of autobattlers, and this one actually brings something new to the genre. The dynamic market system is a fantastic idea it constantly pushes you to adapt instead of forcing the same solved builds every game. Seeing popular strategies become more expensive naturally keeps the meta moving without relying on endless balance patches. There's a surprising amount of depth in the interactions between minions, spells, relics, and positioning. Every run feels like you're solving a different puzzle, and the async PvP works really well if you don't always have time for live matches. It's clear a lot of thought went into the core design. If you enjoy strategy games that reward experimentation and adapting on the fly instead of memorizing a tier list, this is absolutely worth checking out. Looking forward to seeing how it grows.

Big fan so far. I really enjoy making a selection for your team and spells, rather than mechanics I'm more used to in auto battlers with rarity based rankings of units but all being technically available. Knowing what units you can have, and then trying to use your selection of units and spells to build from and counter the other teams on is a lot of fun. The price changes of units and spells based on use is a really interesting mechanic, and I'm curious how the levers are working in the background to make it happen. But it means, despite the fact that you can build your own team more than in other auto battlers I've played, you still can't necessarily focus on one build - you need to be paying attention to the meta changes going on in real time and whether its worth swapping things around based on price. The investment mechanic is just there for fun right now, and while it is absolutely a fun minigame to be a little more engaged with the market and unit changes, I'm looking forward to seeing that built upon.

This is such a brilliant idea for the auto-battler genre. The market-based approach to game balance is really fascinating here and this game is really doing something very unique in the auto-battler space as a result. There is live 1v1 PvP and your traditional async PvP and both of these modes work really well. It does feel like some cards perform better in 1v1 than in async, so I'll be curious to see how the market affects both modes. Finally, earning currency so you can bet on the direction the market is going to take is the chef's kiss. This adds a really neat system on top of the auto-battler just to see if you can read which way the meta is going and predict where the market is going to be in a day. Really cool. Dropping an early recommend because I really hope this one gets some good momentum and success because the system is really compelling. Look forward to picking at this one over the next week.
The name of the game is misleading.

If your reading this, I know the question your asking: will it be worth your time and money? Kind of. Its cheap enough that its worth a shot if you like auto battlers. TLDR Pros: Its cheap, has potential, and is built around an interesting concept. It is a "finished" product. It will run on a cell phone. Cons: It shows its a budget game, its got minimal content, and it is very niche. In more depth; I found the game interesting. As you will quickly realize, alot of the game rides on its unique concept; cost of units and spells automatically adjust to the "market". The more a paticular thing is being used, the more quickly the price will adjust. Once in matches, the price is locked in until you return to the main menu and then those costs adjust back to market. This concept makes balance self adjusting - you cant complain about something being "broken" because it will be corrected in short order. As big brained as this concept is, it will require some fine tuning. I actually found it a little annoying to make a successful run, then find my build was now much more difficult to pull off because the market had increased the price of my build while i was playing. The shifting meta was too fast and started becoming frustrating. Its a skill cap, but I can see it actually turning off alot of people. Maybe slowing it down a little to a daily/weekly thing might be better for us oldies? The actual gameplay is in all honesty fairly vanilla. Auto battlers are usually a bit dry in this sense by virtue of the genre so i can forgive it to a degree, but If your going to be watching things doing the fighting, it helps if its amusing to watch - things that are polished or layered upon in other games and autobattlers, such as the visibility of attacks, explosions or special effects, are very much absent here. Most things just swing their fists, which is not paticularily entertaining, and frequently difficult to see. Special abilities that summon or have effects have no animations or clear indicators. Units that have been "enhanced" by spells have no additional visual indicators, and the more units the more of a confusing mess it starts to be. Another small but annoying thing; units will change targets to whatever is the "weakest" unit in range. In other battlers once on a target they often "lock" in until that enemy is dead. Its a small detail, but this makes having a front line important, and positioning matters more. Not here. When your softer back line runs in, they are just automatically shot down or beat down by the surrounding units unless a unit flagged as a "tank" is nearby specifically to tank. Another mechanic that seems to be lacking; no "teams" or "class" synergies to create exploitable combos between units that normally would have no synergy, but might share a theme. Hopefully this is added in some form later. The unit design and spells seem to be intentionally tepid; they have no real theme and the designs seem intended for simplicity, possibly out of necessity. They are all kind of generic, inoffensive and cutesy which doesnt jive with the idea that they are battling to the death. Music and sound effects are simple and emphasize the "budget" nature of the game. While people hardly play auto-battlers for deep stories, background or philosophical answers it would go a long way here if units actually had a few details. It very much seems like a strategic game with a casual phone game skin. One other minor thing; I get its the name of your studio, but the name of the game is a bit too on the nose, You could have thought of something a bit more appealing or catchy yea? Like Awsome Tactics, or Sandbox Tactics, or Wall Street Tactics? Anyways, its fun for what it is, its cheap, and it has potential - but it begs for more refinement and polish. Worth a shot/10
REALLY good. It needs more depth though. I'm hoping there will be more content added because the live market idea is brilliant for balancing. I wonder why more games don't do this.

Pretty cool auto battler. I love the market system which is keeping the meta from getting stale. It felt good using the cheaper overlooked units to win. I'm excited to see how the meta develops and what new units are going to be added. GG
Unit and spell prices changing dynamically as a concept is done far better here than I would have expected, fun game and it will be very interesting to see how new units/spells impact the game
Fun take on an auto-battler. The graphics are fun, and the market system is one of the most innovative things I have seen in a while. One of those games where you want to just play one more round!

Very Fun interesting mechanic with the units always changing prices to balance out the game, really enjoying it my brother Bought it for my birthday and then went out and purchased it for himself. found out about it from Pastor Druski's stream
a bit lack luster in relation to a auto battler game

I'm honestly pretty bad at this game, which I think i find the most frustrating part, but the market dynamics are cool, and other than wishing we had a bit more money per round, i think it's a simple, with surprisingly good depth auto battler. as i'm sure others have commented the market dynamics can change the game a lot. and require adaptabillity. Cards that I was using on day one, and going (i'm so op), the next day had more than tripled in cost, cause everyone realized the same thing, and guess what, I looked slightly less op.
Simple but really interesting, feels almost like a social experiment.

The following issues have been resolved, and the feedback from the producer is very prompt! Please remove the moving black and white chess pieces queue below, as it looks very uncomfortable to watch. Alternatively, could you add a hidden option? Thank you to the production team. The mana and money systems are quite interesting, as is the dynamic pricing in stock investment, which has its own unique flavor. Additionally, there are issues specific to this type of auto-chess game, such as insufficient visibility of action lines, making it difficult to quantify the impact of players' decisions on the outcome of the game. Both winning and losing are somewhat inexplicable. The future looks promising, with more units and spells to come. The moving checkerboard formation is really unnecessary. In addition, the PvP room battle mode is also needed for promoting new content.

OK just a couple hours in and instantly loving this game - love the weird creatures and the interesting ballancing mechanic, stops things from going stale. I can see myself racking up triple digit hours in this game 😅

Really unique game concept but not necessarily for deep tactics/auto-battling/creature collecting. There's essentially an in game stock market, the cost of each creature and spell changes with usage/win rate, and then outside of that gameplay you can effectively "bet" (in-game money not real cash) on which ones will increase or decrease value. So for example you may find a good meta with an underutilized creature or spell, see its value is low and "buy the dip." You can also keep playing that meta after investing in an effort to influence stocks you are holding (e.g. someone runs into your build, goes "Oh actually I was overlooking X creature, I'll start taking it more"). Or similarly you can bet that a creature or spell is overvalued and expect that it will go down. The stock market aspect is really the interesting part. The Async PvP autobattler is fine but more of a means to an end. It's like if you ever wanted to bet fake money on whether something gets nerfed (or strengthened), and the nerfing is automated/crowd-sourced.
The game is an absolute gem, but an unpolished one. The dynamic "market" mana system is very interesting.

Great game, dev working really hard to try and make it a fair and fun experience. Balance being handled by a basically live stock market method is unique to the genre and makes the meta change daily, hourly and even by the minute
Fun. Actively developed. The asynchronous PvP aspect of the game means there's no queue times to wait and you also have as much time as you want to puzzle through.
Fun game with a very creative market system

I love the concept of an auto-balancing game with market mechanics ... but the thing is, the dev is also balancing the game via more "traditional" means, with slight changes in wording or mechanics added through patches without patch notes. Maybe they are building towards a "stable" version of the game that will rely fully on the price balancing, but it is frustrating to think a card is currently undervalued, only to realize in game that nobody is playing it because of a stealth nerf. Still recommend yes - it's not expensive and the concept is super cool. EDIT - the dev responded with a perfectly reasonable explanation. Tweaking the game to make it more interesting is always worthwhile, and patch notes will come eventually. Solidifying this as a buy, it's a very unique take on the auto-battler genre and more than worth playing.
